The `name` query parameter keeps only the users whose name contains it as plain text, ignoring case; an empty `name` keeps every user. The `page` and `size` query parameters ask for one page of those users in id order, page 1 holding the first `size` of them. When either is given, the answer is a JSON object with "page", "size", "total" (how many users matched), "pages" (how many pages they fill, 0 when none matched) and "items" (the users on that page); `size` is 10 when only `page` is given and `page` is 1 when only `size` is given, and a page after the last one answers an empty "items". `page` must be a whole number of at least 1 and `size` a whole number from 1 to 100: any other value, an empty one included, answers HTTP 400 with a JSON object whose "error" says what is wrong. Keep the API compatible: without `page` and `size`, GET /users still answers a JSON array of users in id order (every user unless `name` is given), any other query parameter is ignored, and GET /users/:id is unchanged. shared-expenses.prompt: Build a small shared-expenses service in Node.js (no npm dependencies). server.js listens on the port in the PORT environment variable and keeps its data in the JSON file named by the DATA_FILE environment variable, so groups and expenses survive a restart. POST /groups with {"id": "<group id>", "members": ["<name>", ...]} creates a group: 201, 409 if the id exists, and 400 unless members holds at least two distinct non-empty names. POST /groups/<id>/expenses records an expense paid by one member. {"payer": "<name>", "cents": <positive integer>, "split": "equal"} shares it equally among all members, with any cents left over after an even division going one each to the members listed first. {"payer": "<name>", "cents": <positive integer>, "split": "exact", "shares": {"<name>": <cents>, ...}} makes each member listed in shares owe that many whole cents (zero is allowed), and the shares must add up to cents. It answers 201 with {"expense": <n>}, where n is 1 for the group's first expense, then 2, and so on; 400 for an unknown payer or member, a non-positive or non-integer amount, an unknown split, or shares that do not add up. GET /groups/<id>/balances returns an object with each member's net cents, what they paid minus what they owe, so the balances add up to 0. GET /groups/<id>/settlements returns a JSON array of {"from", "to", "cents"} payments that bring every balance to 0: repeatedly the member who owes most pays the member who is owed most the smaller of the two amounts, and ties go to the member listed first. Every route under /groups/<id> answers 404 for an unknown group. Concurrent requests must never lose an expense. Cover the behaviour with node:test tests under test/ that run with `node --test`.

# CloudyBot · Salesforce Multi-Bot Operating Framework & Event-Driven Harness (Target Org: `de`)

Build and deploy **CloudyBot**—a Salesforce-native **multi-bot operating framework and event-driven agent harness**—as a standalone, unmanaged Salesforce DX application in the connected Salesforce Developer Edition org (alias `de`).

Name every metadata component you create in this repository and org with the prefix `CloudyBot` (and `cloudyBot` for Lightning Web Component and Aura bundle names, e.g., `CloudyBot*` Apex classes/objects/tabs/apps/permission sets/groups/custom permissions/remote site settings and `cloudyBot*` LWC bundles).

This prompt specifies **product behavior, architectural constraints, and Salesforce Developer Edition (`de`) environmental physics**—**not** pre-designed Apex class names, custom object/field schemas, internal state-machine status enums, or internal DTO shapes. Inspect org `de` first (live limits, API version `68.0`, Queueable chaining depth, existing metadata, My Domain host, and user permissions), elaborate the state-arrival, concurrency, security, and failure edge cases in your specification, and design the cleanest Salesforce-native architecture that satisfies every constraint below.

---

## 1. Conceptual Model (CloudyBot Framework vs. Bot Instances)

Separate the **framework runtime** cleanly from **instantiated bots**:

- **CloudyBot (Framework / Org Runtime)**: Owns LLM provider connections, default/override endpoint profiles, the Self-Org Salesforce Tooling REST API connection, org-wide active concurrency cap `K`, a single shared scheduled dispatcher, the durable event/task queue, the Org Tool Registry, `1..N` Git Marketplace registrations, hierarchical Org/Group/User governance policies, system-level visual/response/operational settings, rolling retention, and storage backpressure.
- **Bot Instance (Instantiated CloudyBot)**: A first-class org entity with:
  - **Identity**: Stable bot identity, unique case-insensitive `@handle` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,31}$`), display name, description, visual accent/avatar, and lifecycle status (draft, active, paused, archived).
  - **Configuration**: Optional subscription binding to an upstream Bot Definition, local configuration overrides (never clobbered by upstream sync), approved Model Profile selection (within org policy), permitted `@handle` delegates, per-bot enabled skill bindings, tool/CRM/Tooling-API scope restrictions (which may only narrow org/group/user access), and eligible audience (Public Groups / Permission Sets / Users).
  - **Continuity & Isolation**: Support an org/group/user-resolved **default entry bot** and sticky last-active `(bot, thread)` continuity so opening CloudyBot enters chat effortlessly without ceremony, while keeping message history, canonical dialogues, composer drafts, pending cards, and unread badges strictly isolated per user, per bot, and per thread.
- **Bot Definition (Blueprint)**: A portable declarative bot template (locally authored or synced from a Git marketplace) supplying upstream default instructions, identity metadata, requested capabilities, default routines, and recommended skills.
- **Skill (`SKILL.md`)**: A portable, prompt-first instruction package (YAML frontmatter + Markdown body + optional references) stored in Salesforce Files, enabled per bot, invocable via `/<slug>` or progressive tool loading.
- **Org-Stored Tool Definition**: A persisted org record defining a callable tool's JSON schema, target Salesforce surface (`USER_MODE` CRM/SOQL, Salesforce Tooling REST API `v68.0`, Flow, or Harness), execution/approval policy, and handler binding—exposed **both** at the very end of the compiled system message (terminal Layer 5) and in each external provider's native structured `tools[]` parameter so LLM API calls interact concretely with the Salesforce org.
- **Canonical Resumable Dialogue Session (`sessionId`)**: A durable, provider-agnostic ordered transcript (`system` ending with the Exposed Runtime Tools manifest + active tool schema snapshot + ordered `user`, `assistant`, `tool_result`, summary, and steering turns) owned by Salesforce and resumable across Lightning, REST, Flow `@InvocableMethod`, timers, and `@handle` delegations.
- **Marketplace Source (`1..N`)**: An admin-registered Git repository serving Bot Definitions and Skills, supporting deduplicated scheduled pull sync and human-approved bidirectional push.

---

## 2. Hierarchical Governance: Org → Salesforce Public Group(s) → User & Override Matrix

Leverage **native Salesforce governance primitives**—never reinvent parallel auth tables and avoid Hierarchy Custom Settings for group/prompt config (Hierarchy Custom Settings are Profile-only and capped at 255 characters; Protected Custom Settings / admin-only encrypted storage are reserved for write-only secrets alongside Named Credentials):

- **Grouping & Visibility (`Group` / `GroupMember` & OWD-Private Sharing)**:
  - Use **Salesforce Public Groups** for group-wide policies, group-scoped Bot Instances, and group-scoped Marketplaces.
  - Expand `GroupMember` memberships transitively across nested groups (with cycle protection) and give each Group Policy an explicit numeric priority with deterministic tie-breaking.
  - Protect bot, policy, and marketplace visibility with OWD-Private sharing and explicit Apex authorization checks.
- **Entitlements & Field Governance (Permission Sets, Permission Set Groups, Custom Permissions, FLS, `USER_MODE` & Tooling Capabilities)**:
  - Separate capabilities with Custom Permissions assigned via Permission Sets / Permission Set Groups (standard use, CloudyBot org administration, Tooling API schema/read access, Tooling API record mutation access, group/bot authoring, skill authoring, marketplace publishing, and personal prompt/preference overrides).
  - Enforce **FLS** on configuration records so end users cannot mutate org/group guardrails, credentials, endpoint URLs, or sync policies; enforce **`USER_MODE`** CRUD/FLS/sharing on all Salesforce CRM queries and DML; and enforce explicit capability + sObject scope checks on all Salesforce Tooling REST API reads and mutations.
- **Zero-Ceremony Out-of-the-Box Seeding**:
  - Automatically seed the complete Org Tool Registry on initial bootstrap/setup so newly activated bots interact concretely with the Salesforce org immediately out of the box—enabling standard CRM schema/read/SOQL/SOSL/CRUD-proposal tools by default and allowing all `USER_MODE`-accessible queryable/writeable Salesforce objects and fields unless explicitly narrowed by an Org, Public Group, Bot, or User allowlist/denylist (never defaulting tools or CRM scope to empty sets that block every object and field until hand-listed, while shielding internal CloudyBot secret, credential, and governance records from tool mutation or exfiltration).
- **Storage Split (Protecting DE's 5 MB Data Storage vs. 20 MB File Storage)**:
  - Offload large payloads—canonical dialogue transcripts, `SKILL.md` bodies, Bot Definitions, and immutable sync version snapshots—to **Salesforce Files** rather than bloating custom object rows, pairing them with lean indexed metadata rows.
- **Three Deterministic Merge Rules Across `Org → Public Group(s) → User`**:
  1. **Security & Resource Ceilings — Monotonic Narrowing Only** (`Org ∩ Group ∩ User` or `min()`): Approved providers/model profiles, allowed marketplaces and trust tiers, permitted CRM objects/fields/Flows, permitted Tooling API sObjects and Tooling read/write capabilities, allowed credentials, maximum concurrency `K`, max hop/callout ceilings, max `@bot` delegation depth, SOQL row limit ceiling, and mandatory sync/write approval gates. Lower scopes may restrict further, **never widen**.
  2. **Additive / Layered Context — Ordered Layering** (`Org → Group(s) by priority → User`): `systemPromptAppend` segments (within org-configured Group/User character budgets), enabled skills, and available marketplaces (within org ceiling and lock flags).
  3. **Scalar Preferences — Most-Specific-Wins Unless Admin-Locked** (`User > highest-priority Group > Org`): Visual defaults (theme, workspace branding/layout density, Thinking Activity display mode), Response Format defaults (style/verbosity, Markdown/table/citation formatting, structured vs. narrative response types), default entry `@handle`, default triage mode, preferred approved model profile, and notification/coalescing preferences. Any **Admin-Locked** setting prevents Group or User overrides cleanly.
- **Administrative Configuration & Override Matrix**: Make every system-level setting explicitly carry and display its override policy (`Admin-Only`, `Narrow-Only`, `Overridable`, `Admin-Locked`, `Layered`) across six areas:
  1. **Providers, Self-Org Tooling Connection, Credentials & Endpoints (`Admin-Only`)**: Provider enablement, credential bindings (Named Credentials and write-only in-app API keys), default URL vs. provider/model-profile override URLs (e.g., Claude in GovCloud), approved model profile catalog, Self-Org Tooling REST API connection, and live `Test Connection` + `Test Tooling API` verification.
  2. **Visual & Experience Defaults (`Lockable Org Default`)**: Workspace title/branding, accent palette, empty-state welcome & starter prompts, default theme (`Light` | `Dark` | `System`) + user theme-toggle permission, layout density / default rail & Mission-Control drawer state, and **Thinking Activity display mode** (full 3-layer, milestones only, minimal, or hidden + default expand/collapse of `Worked for Xs · N steps`).
  3. **Response Format & Interaction Defaults (`Lockable Org Default` within Admin ceilings)**: Default response style/verbosity (concise vs. detailed, Markdown/tables/citations, structured JSON vs. narrative response types, max output token ceiling), default triage mode (`Auto` | `Quick reply` | `Run in background`) + user triage-steering permission, active-turn coalescing/pill behavior, and record-link / PII-masking display policy.
  4. **Execution, Concurrency, Storage & Operations (`Admin-Only` / `Narrow-Only Ceiling`)**: Org concurrency cap `K`, per-task hop/step cap, per-callout timeout ceiling, max `@bot` delegation depth, SOQL row limit ceiling, rolling retention days, Data/Files backpressure thresholds, manual cleanup, and a **Global Kill Switch / Maintenance Mode** (immediately pauses new dispatches org-wide with a customizable admin notice).
  5. **Security, Tool Registry & Prompt Governance (`Admin-Only Floor` / `Layered`)**: Org CRM object/field ceiling, Tooling API sObject scope & mutation policy, registered Flow allowlist, mandatory human-approval gates (CRM create/update/upsert/delete, Tooling API create/update/delete, skill authoring, Git pushes), Org `systemPromptAppend`, Group/User `systemPromptAppend` budgets, and whether personal user prompt appends are enabled.
  6. **Marketplaces & Sync Governance (`Admin-Only` registration & trust floor)**: `1..N` Git marketplaces, read/write credentials, trust tiers, visibility scopes, default sync cadence/policy, and push/PR permissions.
- **Effective Config & Compiled System Prompt Inspector**: Expose a read-only inspector for any `(User, Bot)` pair showing exact provenance—which Org, Public Group(s), Bot, and User policies contributed each setting, prompt layer, permitted CRM/Tooling scope, enabled skill, reachable `@bot`, marketplace, where any value was narrowed or `Admin-Locked`, and the complete 5-layer compiled system prompt **ending with Layer 5 (Exposed Runtime Tools)**.

---

## 3. 5-Layer System Prompt (Ending with Exposed Tools) & Concrete Org / Tooling API Registry

### 3.1 Real Provider System Channel, 5-Layer Composition & Terminal Exposed Tools Invariant
Send system instructions through **each provider's true system/instructions channel** (OpenAI `instructions` / `system`, Anthropic `system`, Gemini `systemInstruction`, Bedrock `system`, xAI/Grok `role: "system"`, and Native `aiplatform.ModelsAPI` chat `system` role or an explicitly documented generation fallback)—never flatten everything into an unseparated `role: "user"` blob.

Assemble the compiled system message in **5 deterministic layers** with explicit per-layer budgets and deterministic truncation order (**Layer 1 and terminal Layer 5 are never truncated**; only Layers 2–4 trim to budget):

1. **Layer 1 — CloudyBot Platform & Salesforce Environment Base (Immutable by Bot/Group/User Config; Never Truncated)**:
   - Declares that the bot runs inside a Salesforce org (safe org identity, edition, API `68.0`, running user context), names the active **invocation surface** (Lightning App Tab, Lightning Record Page with `recordId`/`objectApiName`, Utility Bar, Authenticated REST API, Flow `@InvocableMethod`, `@handle` delegation, or Scheduled Timer) and supported invocation routes, states active **Response Format** directives, and embeds non-overridable security invariants (`USER_MODE` enforcement, zero self-approval for CRM writes, Tooling API writes, skill edits, or marketplace pushes, and strict delimiting of untrusted CRM records, Tooling payloads, user inputs, and community content as data rather than control instructions).
2. **Layer 2 — Bot Definition Upstream Prompt**: Role, domain expertise, default operating guidelines, and tone from the local or marketplace-synced Bot Definition.
3. **Layer 3 — Configurable `systemPromptAppend` (`Org → Group(s) → User`)**: Ordered system-level appendices for org compliance rules, group terminology/workflows, and user style preferences (when enabled by admin policy). **Upstream marketplace syncs must never overwrite any Layer 3 append.**
4. **Layer 4 — Dynamic Runtime Context (Token-Bounded)**:
   - Reachable `@otherBot` directory (`@handle` + 1-line purpose—filtered to bots permitted for both the calling bot and initiating user) and progressive index of enabled skills (`slug`, `name`, `description`, `/command` trigger only—full `SKILL.md` bodies load on demand).
5. **Layer 5 — Exposed Runtime Tools Manifest (Mandatory Terminal Section of the System Message; Never Truncated)**:
   - **Strict Terminal Placement Invariant**: **The compiled system message prompt must end with Layer 5—the exact tools exposed for this turn.** Nothing (no `systemPromptAppend`, no `@bot` directory, no skill text, no steering note, and **never** compacted historical conversation data) may be appended after Layer 5 in the system channel. Compacted older conversation summaries belong inside the canonical dialogue turn stream, never appended after Layer 5.
   - **Full Canonical Tool Manifest Across All 6 Providers**: Across **every** provider (`Native`, `Grok`, `OpenAI`, `Claude`, `Gemini`, `Bedrock`), emit the full canonical tool manifest at the end of the system message for every enabled and policy-authorized active tool in this `(Org, Public Group(s), Bot, User, Invocation Surface)` session (omitting disabled or unauthorized tools)—including each tool's name, category, target API surface (`USER_MODE` CRM/SOQL vs. Salesforce Tooling REST API `v68.0` vs. Flow vs. Org Operations vs. Harness), execution/approval behavior, concise scope-aware description, full canonical JSON input schema, and concrete Salesforce routing rules (when to inspect CRM vs. Tooling schema first, when to run direct `sf_soql_query` vs. `sf_tooling_query`, and how approval-gated CRM/Tooling mutations stage human-approval diffs and resume). When an org registers more than 25 custom/Flow tools for a session, keep core Salesforce/Tooling/harness tools pinned in Layer 5 and expose a scoped progressive tool-discovery tool—promoting discovered tools' full input schemas into both Layer 5 and `tools[]` on the next turn.
   - **Cross-Provider Synchronization**: Construct native `tools[]` / `toolConfig` on external providers from the exact same filtered tool snapshot rendered in Layer 5, and include a deterministic structured JSON tool-call response contract in Layer 5 for `Native` (`aiplatform.ModelsAPI`) models lacking native `tools[]`.

Include an admin/author **Compiled System Prompt Preview** (with secrets redacted) showing all 5 layers ending with Layer 5 before saving config or applying syncs.

### 3.2 Org-Stored, Runtime-Enriched Tool Registry for Concrete Org & Tooling API Interaction
Store tool definitions as seeded **org records** enriched once per turn from live Salesforce `Schema` and effective policy (computing concise org-scope summaries once per turn rather than repeating long object lists inside every tool schema) so LLM API calls interact **concretely** with the Salesforce org across **both** `USER_MODE` CRM data/SOQL **and** the **Salesforce Tooling REST API (`/services/data/v68.0/tooling/...`)**:

- **Dedicated Direct SOQL & SOSL Tools (`USER_MODE`)**:
  - **`sf_soql_query` (Dedicated Direct Salesforce SOQL Tool)**: Executes read-only SOQL directly against the org in `USER_MODE`. **Do not cripple direct SOQL with brittle custom regex token-whitelists** that reject valid Salesforce syntax: verify the query is a `SELECT`, enforce configured object/field policy ceilings where narrowed, automatically clamp or append a bounded `LIMIT` within the effective row ceiling when omitted or oversized (returning rows plus truncation/count metadata), and support **parent dot-notation joins**, **child relationship subqueries**, **semi-joins / anti-joins**, **aggregates** (`COUNT()`, `SUM()`, `AVG()`, `MIN()`, `MAX()`, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`), **date literals** (`LAST_N_DAYS:30`, `THIS_QUARTER`), `LIKE`, `IN`, `!=`, `toLabel()`, `ORDER BY`, and `OFFSET`.
  - **`sf_sosl_search`**: Cross-object keyword search in `USER_MODE` with proper SOSL reserved-character escaping (handling emails, domains, hyphens, and phone fragments cleanly).
- **CRM Schema Exploration & Direct Record Read (`USER_MODE`)**:
  - **`sf_discover_schema` & `sf_describe_sobject`**: Searchable, paginated discovery of accessible Standard and Custom sObjects across the full org `Schema` (never cutting off alphabetically at the first 100 `A*` standard objects and hiding `Contact`, `Opportunity`, `Case`, or `Lead`), plus per-object CRUD flags, Record Types, accessible fields, picklist values, external-ID flags, and parent/child relationship names.
  - **`sf_get_record`**: Direct single-record read in `USER_MODE` by sObject and record ID (essential on Lightning Record Pages).
- **Concrete CRM Record Create, Update, Upsert & Delete (Human-Approval-Gated `USER_MODE` DML)**:
  - **`sf_create_record`, `sf_update_record`, `sf_upsert_record` (supporting external-ID fields), and `sf_delete_record`**: Build immutable, versioned, precondition-checked **Approval Proposals** (with `USER_MODE` before/after field diffs) and park for explicit human confirmation—never silently mutating CRM. Upon confirmation, execute the real `USER_MODE` create/update/upsert/delete, append the committed receipt into the dialogue `tool_result`, and continue the LLM turn.
- **Salesforce Tooling REST API — Schema Exploration, Direct Tooling SOQL & Record Create / Update / Delete (`/services/data/v68.0/tooling/...`)**:
  - Backed by real authenticated HTTP callouts to `/services/data/v68.0/tooling/...` (**never** faked with a hardcoded local `ApexClass` table query):
  - **`sf_tooling_describe`**: Explores the Tooling-exposed API schema—listing Tooling sObjects (`/tooling/sobjects/`) or describing a specific Tooling entity (`/tooling/sobjects/{type}/describe`, e.g., `EntityDefinition`, `FieldDefinition`, `ValidationRule`, `Flow`, `FlowDefinition`, `CustomObject`, `CustomField`, `ApexClass`, `ApexTrigger`, `ApexCodeCoverageAggregate`, `LightningComponentBundle`, `FlexiPage`, `ApexLog`, `MetadataComponentDependency`, `TraceFlag`, `DebugLevel`), including field schemas, `Metadata` sub-schemas, relationships, and CRUD flags.
  - **`sf_tooling_query`**: Executes validated read-only Tooling SOQL directly against `/services/data/v68.0/tooling/query/?q=...` (with cursor pagination and actionable guidance when Salesforce Tooling requires single-record retrieval for `Metadata`/`FullName`/`SymbolTable` fields).
  - **`sf_tooling_get_record`**: Fetches single Tooling records (`/tooling/sobjects/{type}/{id}` for `Metadata`, `FullName`, `SymbolTable`, `Formula`, or `Markup`) and bounded debug log bodies (`/tooling/sobjects/ApexLog/{id}/Body`).
  - **`sf_tooling_create_record`, `sf_tooling_update_record`, and `sf_tooling_delete_record`**: Create, update, and delete permitted Tooling API records via HTTP `POST`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` on `/services/data/v68.0/tooling/sobjects/{type}...` (e.g., `ValidationRule`, `CustomField`, `TraceFlag`, `DebugLevel`, `ApexLog`, `MetadataContainer` workflows). Stage an immutable, precondition-checked before/after diff proposal (blocking mutation or exfiltration of CloudyBot credentials or governance metadata) and, upon authorized human confirmation, execute the Tooling HTTP mutation in a callout-safe boundary, record the receipt in `tool_result`, and continue the LLM turn.
- **Org Limits, Flow Integration & Harness Tools**:
  - **`sf_org_limits`** (live org limit usage and headroom across API, Data/File storage, async Apex, Platform Events, and streaming), **`sf_invoke_flow`** (admin-allowlisted Autolaunched Flows honoring per-Flow immediate vs. approval policy and returning Flow output variables in `tool_result`), plus harness tools for `@handle` bot delegation, progressive `SKILL.md` loading, human-approved skill drafting, one-shot/recurring timers, bounded subtask fan-out, mid-task human clarification, and marketplace sync.

---

## 4. Canonical Resumable Dialogue, 6-Provider Adapters & Endpoint URL Resolution

### 4.1 Salesforce-Owned Resumable Dialogue (`sessionId`)
- Persist the ordered canonical dialogue in Salesforce Files linked from a lean session index, supporting optional `sessionId` (continue in place) or `seedFromSessionId` (fork context) across every entry surface (Lightning, REST, Flow `@InvocableMethod`, queued tasks, timers, and `@bot` delegations).
- **Atomic Turn-Group Compaction & Strict Validation**: Compact older turns into bounded summaries inside the turn stream (**never** appended after Layer 5 in the system message, and **never** splitting an assistant `tool_call`/`tool_use` from its matching `tool_result`). Reject unrecognized tool names or unknown actions cleanly—never mark unknown actions completed.

### 4.2 Six Providers, Named Model Profiles & 3-Tier Endpoint URL Resolution
Support **Named Provider / Model Profiles** so an org can run multiple endpoints per provider simultaneously with zero hardcoded secrets:
1. **Native Salesforce LLM (`aiplatform.ModelsAPI`)**: In-org readiness probe + one-click activation; structured JSON tool-call adapter driven by Layer 5 when native `tools[]` is absent.
2. **xAI / Grok**: Default URL `https://api.x.ai` (`system` message ending with Layer 5, `tools[]`).
3. **OpenAI / Codex**: Default URL `https://api.openai.com` (`/v1/responses` & `/v1/chat/completions`; `instructions`/`system` ending with Layer 5, `tools[]`, optional `background: true` for >120s waits).

## 5. Event-Driven Harness, Execution Physics, Invocable Actions & `@botName` Collaboration

### 5.1 Real Main-Thread Triage, Steering & Escalation
- Route inbound messages using real LLM/policy triage (not hardcoded keyword stubs), supporting explicit user toggles (*"Run in background"* / *"Quick reply"*) when permitted and a **"Send to background task"** action on any quick reply to promote that reply and its dialogue into a tracked background task.

### 5.2 Timeout-Safe Multi-Hop Execution, Callout Ordering, DE Chain Depth & Principal Safety
Design the async execution loop around Salesforce's real transaction physics:
- **120s Callout Ceiling & Uncommitted-Work Restriction**: Never trap multi-turn LLM + tool loops inside one Apex transaction, and never perform DML, row locks, or savepoints before an outbound HTTP callout in the same transaction (which fails in Salesforce with `uncommitted work pending`—ensure LLM, Tooling REST, and Git HTTP callouts execute in a clean callout-first boundary before persisting results).
- **Multi-Tool Batching & Developer Edition Queueable Chain-Depth 5 Resilience**: Batch independent tool calls from the same assistant turn sensibly within governor and callout-ordering rules, avoid wasting a separate Queueable hop on triage when already running asynchronously, and handle Developer Edition's **5-depth Queueable chaining cap** gracefully—checkpointing remaining work back to the durable queue before hitting stack-depth exhaustion so the next client continuation poll or scheduled dispatch resumes a fresh chain at depth 0 without crashing.
- **Honest Principal Boundaries**: In Salesforce, `USER_MODE` enforces the actual running user's rights (`System.runAs` is test-only and storing a user ID does not confer impersonation). Preserve the initiating user's principal across interactive Queueable chains, and whenever a hop runs under a non-matching system/scheduler/event principal, detect the mismatch at runtime and refuse to run `USER_MODE` CRM or user-scoped operations under that principal—parking protected actions for the initiating user to resume or confirm.

### 5.3 Flow `@InvocableMethod` Ingress (Half-Duplex Sync & Resumable Async)
- Expose an `@InvocableMethod` for Salesforce Flows supporting **`Sync`** (one bounded LLM round-trip reusing `sessionId` if supplied, returning reply text + `sessionId` + `continuationRequired = true`—or auto-queueing when `allowAsyncFallback = true`—if tools, timeout, or prior Flow DML block inline completion) and **`Async`** (immediately queueing onto `sessionId` with zero Flow timeout risk).

### 5.4 Durable Backlog, Concurrency Cap `K`, Steering, Active-Turn Hold, Timers & Quiescence
- **Bounded `K` & Slot-Releasing Waits**: Drain queued tasks across users up to org cap `K` (default 3) with priority, FIFO tie-breaking, dependency readiness, per-user fairness, and Global Kill Switch support. Tasks waiting on timers, >120s provider jobs, child subtasks, human clarification/approval, or peer bots **must release their concurrency slot**.
- **Boundary Steering & Cascading Cancel**: Apply versioned `steer` amendments at the next step boundary, surface partial-failure summaries on fan-out subtasks, and cascade cancellations cleanly while fencing stale attempts.
- **Two-Layer Context-Aware Delivery**: Hold and coalesce concurrent completions or timer outputs targeting a `sessionId` while a user turn or tool group is open on the server, and show a non-disruptive **"New update ready"** pill in Lightning when the user has an unsent composer draft.
- **Single Shared Scheduler & Idle Quiescence**: Consolidate all one-shot/recurring timers, expired-lease recovery sweeps, and scheduled marketplace syncs onto **one shared scheduled job** (respecting DE's 5-job limit) that unschedules itself to **zero scheduled/queued jobs when idle**.

### 5.5 `@botName` Cross-Bot Referencing & Collaboration
- Support `@` composer autocomplete (ignoring emails, URLs, and code blocks), multi-mention specialist fan-out returning speaker-attributed synthesis, and bot-to-bot delegation enforcing **permission intersection** (caller bot's allowed delegates ∩ initiating user's bot eligibility, with CRM access still bound to the initiating user's `USER_MODE`), slot-releasing waits, cycle/depth guards, and cascading cancel.

## 6. Skills System (Enable, Create, Update & Progressive Disclosure)

- Store `SKILL.md` artifacts (YAML frontmatter + Markdown body) in Salesforce Files with org-wide and bot-local bindings, `/` composer autocomplete (`/<slug>` or `/<marketplace>:<slug>` on collision), and on-demand progressive loading so Layer 4 stays compact.
- Prompt-first only (never execute downloaded scripts in Apex). Validate declared required Salesforce objects, Tooling sObjects, tools, and Flows against **effective policy plus live `USER_MODE` `Schema` / Tooling accessibility** on enable and sync (working seamlessly with default-accessible CRM scope). Require **explicit human approval** via a versioned draft diff card (with rollback history) whenever a bot proposes creating or editing a skill.

## 7. Multi-Marketplace Git Federation (`1..N` Repos) & Two-Way Scheduled Sync

- **Federated Sources**: Register `1..N` Git marketplaces via Named/External Credentials (GitHub, GitLab, or HTTPS catalog—zero hardcoded tokens) with unique `<marketplaceSlug>/<itemSlug>` addressing, `Internal` | `Community` trust tiers, Org vs. Public Group visibility, `PullOnly` | `Bidirectional` sync direction, and cross-marketplace skill dependencies restricted to registered sources.
- **Deduplicated Pull & Safe 3-Way Merge**: Check each `(marketplace, ref)` once per sync window via `ETag`/commit SHA (0 DML on unchanged no-op) with per-repo backoff isolation; preserve Org/Group/User `systemPromptAppend` and local bot overrides with visible drift notices; **hold any capability-expanding upstream update for explicit Admin approval**; pin in-flight runs to their starting snapshot; support **Rollback** and **Detach / Fork locally**; and preserve live bots/threads if an upstream item is removed.
- **Two-Way Push / `PullRequest`**: On `Bidirectional` marketplaces, publish approved local Skills/Bot Definitions + updated `marketplace.json` via branch + `PullRequest` (or admin direct commit) after explicit human diff approval, automatic privacy/secret/org-ID/`systemPromptAppend` stripping, remote `HEAD` SHA divergence conflict checks (never force-push), immutable push receipts, and anti-echo sync tracking.

## 9. Developer Edition Constraints, Tri-Surface Mock Transports & Acceptance Scenarios

5. **Event & API Ceilings (`DailyDeliveredPlatformEvents = 10000`, `StreamingApiConcurrentClients = 20`, `DailyAsyncApexExecutions = 250000`, `DailyApiRequests = 15000`)**: Content-free Platform Events, `ETag`/SHA marketplace deduplication, and bounded LWC polling/catch-up.
